rationale: Per-drug signal strength varies a lot (strong for targeted oncology drugs, near-noise for many non-oncology ones), so one shared alpha=5000 over-shrinks some drugs and under-shrinks others. I'm swapping in efficient leave-one-out (GCV) RidgeCV that picks a separate alpha for each drug on the training fold only. It uses the same features and is still one fast closed-form multi-output fit. I haven't run this candidate, so its Dev score is unknown.

A lot of PRISM sensitivity follows lineage. In the current model that signal is spread thinly over 5,000 genes that are all shrunk heavily at alpha=5000. This change adds one-hot OncotreeLineage columns scaled by a weight w, so the lineage effect is penalised much less than single genes. w is chosen by grouped inner CV on the training fold only, and w=0 is one of the options, so the model can fall back to the current solution. I haven't run this candidate, so its Dev score is unknown.

Many PRISM drugs share a few response axes, such as general cytotoxic or proliferation sensitivity and lineage programs. For weak drugs, each drug's own ridge prediction is mostly noise, so I'm turning the ridge into a reduced-rank ridge. Predictions are projected onto the top-k right singular vectors of the fitted drug×line response, which pools signal across similar drugs. k is chosen by grouped inner CV on the training fold only, and full rank is one of the options, so the model can fall back to the current solution. I haven't run this, so its Dev score is unknown.

The current ridge treats each drug's own target genes like the other 5,000 variable genes, so it shrinks them heavily (or drops them if their variance is low). Yet target expression is the most direct biological sensitivity marker for targeted drugs such as EGFR, BRAF or BCL2 inhibitors. This change adds each drug's target-gene expression (from `ctx["drugs"].target`) through a per-drug kernel ridge, `K = XXᵀ + w·T_dT_dᵀ`, so target genes are penalised `w` times less than other genes. One shared `w` is chosen by grouped inner CV on the training fold only, and `w=0` is one of the options, which reproduces the current model exactly. I haven't run this, so its Dev score is unknown.
